subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>, Platform SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Aisha / FintechCo SRE team —

Thanks again for taking the time to go through the demo today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the performance/SLO items we discussed and propose next steps so we can qualify Redwood against your production requirements. Attached is a filled SLO checklist and a recording of today’s demo for reference.

Key SLOs we heard today (please confirm):
- Latency target: P95 ≤ 300 ms for text-generation endpoints
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 req/s, peak bursts up to 500 req/s
- Concurrency: ~50 active concurrent sessions (peaks to 60)
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for the web UI (partial results important)
- Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx under expected load

Clarifying requests from our side:
- Typical request/response token sizes (avg input / avg output)
- Sample QPS traces (1-hour and 24-hour) and any peak windows
- Any network egress constraints or private VPC requirements for early testing

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) FintechCo: share load profile and sample requests (Aisha / SRE) — due EOD 9/16
2) Redwood: provision trial Dedicated capacity and run a 48-hour soak with your load profile (owner: Connor) — propose 9/20 start
3) Redwood Infra: run scale tests and produce latency/throughput report (owner: Marcus) — deliverable 9/22
4) Decision meeting: review results and confirm fit / next procurement steps — propose 9/23

Can you confirm the SLO values above and the timeline? If anything needs to be stricter (e.g., P95 < 250 ms), call it out and we’ll adjust the test plan.

Attachments: FintechCo_SLO_checklist_v1.xlsx, demo-recording-20270913.mp4

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO checklist & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few quick confirmations and questions: 

- The SLOs you listed look right as a starting point. Our target for external-facing UI is P95 <= 250 ms ideally, but we can evaluate at 300 ms as a baseline for the proof-of-concept.
- Baseline traffic is ~150 req/s; we see daily spikes up to ~400-500 req/s during end-of-day batch windows.
- Concurrency: 45 typical, up to 60 during spikes.
- Streaming: yes, token-level streaming is required for chat UX.
- Error budget: we expect <0.5% 5xx for any vendor.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you support chunked/token streaming over HTTP/2 or WebSocket today? Any caveats on throughput when streaming is on?
2) What pre-built configs do you recommend for model batching / KV cache for a workload with avg input ~100 tokens / avg output ~300 tokens?

We’ll attach a short 1-hour sample QPS trace and a CSV of representative requests — I’ll send that to you by tomorrow EOD. Looping in our SRE for the technical numbers.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product (Integrations) | FintechCo
aisha.khan@fintechco.com

From: Platform SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO checklist & next steps

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 15:02, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Key SLOs we heard today (please confirm):
> - Latency target: P95 ≤ 300 ms for text-generation endpoints

Confirmed and adding specifics from our telemetry: 
- Baseline: 140-160 req/s (avg 1hr); typical QPS during business hours ~180 req/s
- Peak observed (24hr window): short bursts to ~520 req/s (10-15 minute windows)
- Concurrency: sustained 50-55, short peaks to ~65
- Typical payload: avg input ~120 tokens, avg output ~300 tokens; 95th percentile output tokens ~800 in some flows
- Streaming is required for our web chat; partial results must be delivered to the client within 150-200 ms ideally
- Network: instances are in GCP us-east1; we'll provide access for testing via a bastion or temporary IP allowlist

We will upload a representative 1-hour trace and a 24-hour QPS CSV to the shared drive (link to follow). For the soak, we can provide a synthetic load script or allow Redwood to replay the trace.

-- SRE

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>, Platform SRE <sre@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T02:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance SLO checklist & next steps

Thanks Aisha and team — this is super helpful. Based on the numbers you provided we'll run two test profiles:

1) Baseline steady-state: 180 req/s for 48 hours to validate stability and error rates
2) Peak burst test: replay 15-minute high-QPS windows (up to 520 req/s) across the 48-hour run to measure tail latency under burst conditions

Initial Redwood test config we propose:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with autoscale headroom to cover 1.5x peak
- Batching: adaptive batching tuned to maintain P95 <= 300 ms; we'll start with target batch sizes of 8-16 depending on model latency
- KV/prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts to reduce token compute
- Quantization profile: FP16 or INT8 where supported for cost/latency tradeoffs (Marcus will validate model compatibility)

Decision criteria we suggest for the POC:
- Meet P95 <= 300 ms for >= 95% of requests during baseline profile
- Error rate < 0.5% for 48-hour run
- Successful streaming: first partial token delivered within 200 ms for >= 95% of streaming requests

Action items (owners):
- FintechCo: share 1-hour and 24-hour traces + allowlist for test (Aisha / SRE) — due 9/16
- Redwood: provision Dedicated trial and schedule test (Connor) — plan to start 9/20
- Redwood Infra: validate quantization/benchmark for target model(s) (Marcus) — deliver 9/22
- All: Decision call 9/23 to review test artifacts and decide next steps

If the compressed timeline works for you I'll have Connor send the trial env details and Marcus will follow up on the model/quantization notes.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
